# Run comparison view with parameter/metric diff highlighting

## Description

Delivers the experiment comparison capability in the Dashboard: users select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side, and when comparing two runs, the values that changed between them are highlighted. This gives data scientists in-platform visibility into what differs between candidate training and pipeline runs, replacing the current workflow of exporting run data to spreadsheets for comparison and supporting model promotion decisions with side-by-side evidence.

## Scope

- Multi-run selection from the Dashboard runs list: a user can select two or more runs and invoke a comparison.
- A comparison view presenting each selected run's parameters and metrics side by side.
- Diff highlighting within the comparison view: when two runs are compared, parameters and metrics that changed between the two runs are visually distinguished from unchanged ones.
- Run data (parameters, metrics) is consumed through the interfaces that already back the existing per-run pages. The strategy requires no Data Science Pipelines code changes; Data Science Pipelines is a passive component here, validated through the acceptance criteria below.
- Out of scope per the strategy: automatic best-run selection or promotion, and comparison across clusters or across projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a user viewing the runs list, when they select two or more runs and invoke the comparison action, then a comparison view opens showing each selected run's parameters and metrics side by side (measured by: the values shown match those on the corresponding per-run pages).
- Given a comparison of exactly two runs, then every parameter and metric key present in the comparison is classified and presented as changed or unchanged between the two runs, so the user can see at a glance which values differ.
- Given a run selected for comparison whose parameters or metrics include a key absent from another selected run, then the comparison presents the gap without error.
- Given runs retrieved through the existing Data Science Pipelines run interfaces, the comparison displays the same parameters and metrics as the existing per-run pages (passive-component validation for Data Science Pipelines).
- The Dashboard build and existing test suite remain green with the changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard — fully covered by this epic.
- HLR-3 (P1): a run "diff" view highlighting which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs — covered as a rendering mode of this epic's comparison view. HLR-1 and HLR-3 overlap in wording (requirements consolidated from two customer councils); both are delivered by this single comparison surface rather than duplicated across epics.

# Run lineage links on registered model versions

## Description

Delivers the Model Registry side of run-to-model traceability: a registered model version records the run that produced it, and that reference is exposed through the Model Registry's supported interfaces so clients — including the Dashboard — can navigate from a registered version back to the experiment run behind it. This is the data foundation that lets a comparison be opened from the Model Registry and gives model promotion decisions a direct link from a candidate version to the parameters and metrics of its producing run.

## Scope

- Define and implement how a model version carries a reference to the run that produced it. The platform architecture identifies custom properties on model versions as the extension point for attaching structured metadata; the concrete mechanism (custom-property convention or another supported representation) is the implementing team's design decision.
- Ensure the run reference is captured when a model version is registered from a run, and is readable back through the Model Registry REST API.
- The run reference identifies a run within the same project — cross-cluster and cross-project linkage is out of scope per the strategy.
- Existing model versions without a recorded run reference remain valid and unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered from a producing run, then the model version exposes a reference to that run that is retrievable through the Model Registry REST API (measured by: an API query on the model version returns the run reference).
- Given the run reference on a model version, then it is sufficient for a client to identify the corresponding run in the platform's run listing, so a comparison can be opened against it.
- Given a model version with no recorded run reference (for example, registered before this capability existed), then the model version remains fully functional and simply carries no reference.
- Existing Model Registry API behavior and entity compatibility are preserved; the Model Registry build and test suite remain green with the changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): registered model versions link back to the run that produced them — registry data side, owned by the Model Registry team. The user-facing part of HLR-2 (opening a comparison from the Model Registry UI) is delivered separately by the Dashboard team and consumes the reference this epic provides.

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry

## Description

Delivers the Dashboard side of registry-driven comparison: from a registered model version in the Model Registry UI, a user can open the run comparison view seeded with the run that produced the version, and continue selecting further runs for side-by-side comparison and diffing from there. This connects model promotion workflows to the experiment evidence behind each candidate version, so reviewers do not have to leave the platform to compare the runs a model came from.

## Scope

- Surface the producing-run reference on a model version in the registry UI.
- A comparison entry point on the model version that opens the run comparison view with the linked run included among the selected runs.
- Graceful handling when no run reference is recorded on a version, or the linked run is no longer available or accessible — no broken navigation.
- The comparison opened from the registry is the same comparison experience available from the runs list (same view, same side-by-side presentation, same diff highlighting).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version with a recorded producing-run reference, when the user invokes the comparison action from the model version, then the run comparison view opens with the linked run included among the selected runs.
- Given a model version with no recorded run reference, then the registry presents no broken comparison entry point (the action is unavailable or accompanied by an explanatory state).
- Given a model version whose linked run no longer exists or is not accessible to the user, then the user receives a clear message rather than an error state.
- Given a comparison opened from the registry, then it offers the same side-by-side parameter/metric presentation and two-run diff highlighting as a comparison started from the runs list.
- The Dashboard build and existing test suite remain green with the changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): "so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry" — the user-facing entry point in the registry UI, owned by the Dashboard team. It builds on the run comparison view and on the producing-run reference that the Model Registry records on model versions (the Model Registry team's deliverable), both of which are prerequisites of this epic.
